subject: Structured multi-year prepay options + early-termination redline
messages:
From: Sara Kramer <sara.kramer@nimbuspay.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@nimbuspay.com>, procurement@nimbuspay.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring multi-year prepay with ramp — initial questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. NimbusPay is excited about the latency profiles you showed. Our leadership asked for a couple of concrete pricing structures we can review with finance:

- A multi-year prepay with step-up (year 1 lower usage ramping into year 2/3)
- Clarification on refunds or credits if actual consumption undershoots the committed ramp
- How co-terming would work if we bring additional business under a single contract later

Attached is a simple monthly forecast and our preferred ramp assumptions. Can you share 1) a clean term sheet with examples and 2) what the legal redline would look like for early termination/refund mechanics?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like to review by Friday.

Best,
Sara
Sara Kramer
Head of Platform Operations, NimbusPay
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: Sara Kramer <sara.kramer@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay with ramp — initial questions

Sara — thanks, this is helpful. I attached a draft term sheet with three structured options and a worked example showing refund math under different early-exit scenarios. High-level options:

1) Fixed 3-year prepay (levelized) — best % discount, refund via time-pro-rated credits on remaining committed spend, 90-day notice.
2) 3-year stepped prepay (ramp) — year-by-year commit with weighted discounts (year 1 lower discount, years 2–3 higher). Refunds calculated on unused token-dollar value for each remaining year, subject to minimum usage floors.
3) Annual prepay with optional auto-roll (yearly invoice, declining early-exit exposure) — smaller discount, easier co-terming with other purchases.

Key trade-offs to call out: discount vs. liquidity (refunds), minimums for stepped model, and whether refunds are cash or account credit. For sales ops modeling I included the Prepay_Ramp_Model.xlsx so you can change ramp assumptions.

I flagged an early-termination paragraph for legal to propose a conservative redline (see Redline_EarlyTermination.docx). Main asks for you: prefer cash refunds or account credits? Also, do you need an escrow-based holdback for the largest prepay?

Will follow up with legal and finance on exact language.

— Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Kramer <sara.kramer@nimbuspay.com>, Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@nimbuspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay with ramp — initial questions

Alex / team — looped in to propose a redline approach. Quick summary of recommended position:

- For multi-year fixed prepay: allow pro-rata refunds minus an early termination fee equal to 3 months of the committed annualized value OR a fixed % (we prefer fee + pro-rata to limit churn impact).
- For stepped ramp model: calculate refunds per-year bucket. If Year 1 usage < floor (e.g., 60% of committed), apply additional non-refundable portion for Year 1 to cover provisioning costs.
- Refunds: default to account credit unless customer requests cash; cash refunds incur finance approval and up to 30 days processing plus clawback validation.
- Co-terming: allow new line items to co-term at next annual anniversary; provide prorated invoice and apply remaining committed value to co-term calculation.

Please review Redline_EarlyTermination.docx — I added tracked changes and example formulas. Vanessa, any concerns on cash payout exposure? Rishi, can you produce two quick scenarios (cash refund vs credit) for NimbusPay's ramp?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Kramer <sara.kramer@nimbuspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay with ramp — initial questions

Attached is a quick model with three scenarios per Alex's options. Highlights:

- Scenario A (3-year levelized prepaid $3.6M): refund if early-exit in year 2 = $2.4M remaining prepaid value -> after 3-month termination fee (equal to $75k) and clawbacks, net cash refund = $2.325M (if cash requested).
- Scenario B (3-year stepped: $600k yr1 / $1.2M yr2 / $1.8M yr3): if exit at end of year1 with usage at 50% of year1 commit and floor = 60%, non-refundable portion for year1 = 40% of $600k = $240k; remaining refundable across years = $3.6M - $600k - $240k = $2.76M; apply early-exit fee -> net credit/cash difference shown in sheet.
- Scenario C (annual prepay auto-roll $1.2M/yr): refund limited to unused months at invoice rate; minimal processing exposure.

Notes: cash refunds trigger finance review and require proof of consumption and invoice reconciliation. If NimbusPay prefers credits, accounting overhead is lower and we can apply credits to future overages or co-termed expansions.

Model file: Prepay_Ramp_Model.xlsx contains line-by-line formulas. I can export a PDF summary for procurement.

— Rishi Malhotra
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Kramer <sara.kramer@nimbuspay.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@nimbuspay.com>, procurement@nimbuspay.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay with ramp — initial questions

Alex / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the worked examples. Procurement has two quick confirmations:

1) NimbusPay prefers cash refunds for large prepay (>$500k), but is open to account credits for smaller sub-annual adjustments. Will upstream approval if cash refund is requested in negotiation.
2) For co-terming: they want the ability to add one-off projects mid-contract and have those charges either (a) billed separately, or (b) folded into the master agreement at next anniversary with prorated invoice. The legal redline looks reasonable — will propose minor language tweaks (mainly around proof of consumption and dispute timeline).

Action items:
- Alex: update term sheet to show explicit cash refund example for Scenario B (exit end of year1 with usage at 50%).
- Rishi: export a 1-page PDF of the model for procurement (cash vs credit comparison).
- Lauren/Legal: be prepared for a short negotiation on the processing window and escrow requirement (procurement asked if we can put >$1M into a short-term escrow).

We'll aim to circle back Thursday EOD for formal redline.

Best,
Sara
